Title: Ningde rises as global lithium battery powerhouse | govt.chinadaily.com.cn
### govt.chinadaily.com.cn. # Ningde rises as global lithium battery powerhouse. Ningde, a coastal city in Fujian province, reported that output from its lithium battery and stainless steel industrial clusters surpassed 300 billion yuan ($43.06 billion) and 240 billion yuan in 2025 respectively. Starting from scratch, the city, named "China's New Energy Battery Capital", cemented its position as the world's largest production base for polymer lithium-ion batteries. That shift began in 2011, when Contemporary Amperex Technology Co Ltd (CATL), a leading lithium-ion battery maker, was founded, yet the city lacked supporting manufacturers for key battery materials. Local authorities and leading firms moved to expand the supply chain, attracting projects in cathode and anode materials, coated separators, electrolytes, battery components, and intelligent equipment manufacturing. By the end of 2025, Ningde had established a comprehensive industrial ecosystem. CATL's production bases in the city now have a total capacity of 330 gigawatt-hours (GWh), with another 170 GWh under construction or planned. More than 90 upstream and downstream companies have clustered locally, enabling one-stop production spanning raw materials, research and development, and manufacturing. Throughout the 14th Five-Year Plan (2021-25), Ningde maintained its spot among China's top 100 cities for advanced manufacturing. Its power battery cluster was also designated a national advanced manufacturing cluster, underscoring the city's growing role in China's high-end manufacturing landscape. ### MOST POPULAR. ### Editors' Picks. HomeContentNingde: The Heart of the Lithium Battery Revolution. # Ningde: The Heart of the Lithium Battery Revolution. In the coastal city of Ningde, Fujian province, a remarkable transformation is underway. Once an overlooked locale, it has emerged as a global powerhouse in lithium battery production. With output from its industrial clusters surpassing 300 billion yuan (approximately $43 billion) by 2025, Ningde has rightfully earned the title of 'China's New Energy Battery Capital.' This evolution began in 2011 with the founding of Contemporary Amperex Technology Co Ltd (CATL), which quickly became a leader in lithium-ion battery manufacturing. Initially lacking essential suppliers for key materials like cathodes and anodes, local authorities and businesses rallied to build a robust supply chain. As I delve into this narrative, I can't help but marvel at how far Ningde has come. Just over a decade ago, few would have predicted that this city would become synonymous with cutting-edge energy solutions. Today, CATL’s innovations are not just about powering electric vehicles; they represent a shift towards sustainable energy practices worldwide. The heart of CATL's operations lies within its advanced research facilities like the 21C Lab—a hub dedicated to next-generation battery technologies. Here researchers explore ways to enhance efficiency and longevity while reducing environmental impact—a pressing concern as we navigate climate change challenges. As consumers increasingly rely on devices powered by these batteries—from smartphones to electric cars—the implications extend beyond mere convenience; they touch upon our collective responsibility toward sustainability and innovation. Interestingly enough, while discussing batteries often conjures images of mundane gadgets or automotive power sources, their significance runs deeper than that. Batteries are now central players in discussions about renewable energy storage systems and grid stability—key components needed for transitioning away from fossil fuels.
